name: Garmin Kansas City Marathon
summary: The Garmin Kansas City Marathon is held on the third Saturday of October. The recent course starts at Frank A. Theis Park, across from the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, and tours the city. Runner reviews call the hills tough, and race listings give different climb totals.
courseHighlights: Start at Frank A. Theis Park by the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
Kauffman Center for the Performing Arts and Union Station
18th & Vine, with the Finish Line Festival back at Theis Park

paceStrategy.summary: Runners describe the hills as inconsistent, with long climbs in the second half, including a long one on Ward Parkway. Start slower than goal pace and run the hills by effort.

segments.terrain: Start area, downtown and the WWI Memorial area
segments.advice: Run slower than goal pace; the first miles include early climbs.
Hold effort, not pace, over the rolling hills.

segments.terrain: Ward Parkway area, with a long climb (runner reports)
segments.advice: Expect to slow down; keep your effort steady.
Use the downhill sections and push when you can.

fuelingNotes: The official site lists the course map and Garmin courses but not aid-station details in the pages I read. Take a gel before the hills in the second half, around mile 14 to 15.
tips: The route changes from year to year; use the Garmin course on the official course maps page
The marathon starts early in the morning, so plan your travel to the start
Reviews report a short climb right before the finish line

faq.question: Is the Kansas City Marathon hilly?
faq.answer: Yes. Race listings and runner reviews describe a hilly course with long climbs, and the totals vary between sources, so no number is given here.

faq.question: When is the Kansas City Marathon held?
faq.answer: It is held on the third Saturday of October.

faq.question: Where does the Kansas City Marathon start?
faq.answer: The recent course starts at Frank A. Theis Park, across from the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art.
